post.contentHtml:
Earnings grew, but the share price moved the other way

No.1 (code 3562), listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, sells and maintains multifunction printers, business telephones, and security equipment for small and mid-sized businesses. Its latest share price is 1,558 yen (based on data as of November 13). That is about 29.8% lower than a year ago. While writing this article, I could not confirm the closing price for November 17 on the web. Please treat this price as the value from the previous trading day.

The share price fell sharply, yet the earnings trend over the same period was not bad. This mismatch is the most noticeable point about this stock right now.

Confirmed earnings trend

ItemDetails
Fiscal year ended February 2026 (full year)Sales of about 17.5 billion yen (up about 23% year on year), ordinary profit of about 1.39 billion yen (up about 34.5%)
Company forecast for fiscal year ending February 2027Ordinary profit of about 1.59 billion yen (up about 14.1%)
Q1 of fiscal year ending February 2027 (March–May)Sales and ordinary profit rose from a year earlier, but net profit declined
First half of fiscal year ending February 2027 (March–August)According to one summary, sales up about 6.7% and ordinary profit up about 163%. Figures differ by source, so checking the original filing is necessary

Ordinary profit is core operating profit plus or minus non-operating items such as interest income. It is a metric often used to gauge a company's regular earning power.

Possible reasons for the weak share price

The following are estimates, not confirmed facts.

  • Quality of earnings concerns: Some analyses point out that profit growth is slower than sales growth. There are also mentions of losses on investments in anonymous partnerships (private investment contracts). This may be why net profit has not kept pace with the sharp rise in ordinary profit.
  • Thin trading volume: The median annual trading value is about 44 million yen. Daily trading is very thin, so even small sell orders can move the price significantly, and it is hard for institutional investors to get in.
  • Nature of the business: Selling and maintaining multifunction printers is a mature market. It may be a structure in which growth expectations are hard to reflect strongly in the share price.

Business and shareholders

No.1 has two main segments. The Office Consultant segment sells and installs equipment such as multifunction printers, business telephones, and UTM (unified threat management, a single device that bundles multiple security functions). The System Support segment handles maintenance of this equipment and mail-order sales of office supplies. A strength is that equipment sales lead into maintenance rather than ending with a single sale, so recurring revenue tends to build up.

The major shareholders as of October 1 are as follows.

  • Tatsumi Takayuki: 15.07%
  • Credit Saison: 5.12%
  • Employee shareholding: 3.28%
  • Hisamatsu Chihiro: 2.44%
  • Takezawa Kaoru: 1.8%

The largest shareholder holds about 15%, and credit card company Credit Saison holds about 5%. Korea's National Pension Service does not hold this stock.

What to watch next

  • Check the exact first-half interim results and whether net profit followed the rise in ordinary profit.
  • See whether the losses on anonymous partnership investments are one-off or recurring.
  • Whether the full-year ordinary profit forecast of 1.59 billion yen is maintained or raised is also important.
  • Watch whether trading volume increases.

In sum, improving earnings and a falling share price are diverging, and the cause may lie in earnings quality and low liquidity. However, the latest interim details differ by source, so it is hard to draw firm conclusions. Before investing, please check the company's official financial disclosures yourself.
